annotation.title_clean: The Autonomy Aspect of Lethal Autonomous Weapon
annotation.title_en: The Autonomy Aspect of Lethal Autonomous Weapon
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United States (submission to CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS, CCW/GGE.1/2025/WP.6
named_instruments_referenced: Draft articles on autonomous weapon systems (CCW/GGE.1/2024/WP.10)
annotation.summary_en: US working paper to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts proposing how to characterize autonomy in lethal autonomous weapon systems: a capability defined by functions performed without operator intervention after activation, technology-neutral, and usable consistently with IHL in three methods of use, with examples such as loitering munitions and air defence.
key_provisions_or_claims: Autonomy is a capability of the weapon system, so LAWS fall under existing IHL weapon classifications.
Characterize autonomy by functions performed, not specific technologies like machine learning.
A function is autonomous if performed without operator intervention in initiation and execution.
LAWS identify, select and engage targets without further operator intervention after activation.
Reliance on autonomous functions must be in good faith and consistent with distinction, proportionality and precautions.
